transcript.text: How do you decide what to test, when there is never time to test everything?
I'd try to get good code coverage, aim for like eighty percent. I mean, write unit tests for the functions and integration tests for the API endpoints.
Two requests arrive at the same time and both try to update the same record. What can go wrong, and what would you do about it?
There would be a race condition. um, i'd use a lock so only one request can update at a time, or put them in a queue so they get processed one after another.
Explain something technical you have worked on to someone who is smart but not an engineer.

I'd use an analogy. Like if I was explaining an API I'd say it's like a waiter in a restaurant, you tell them what you want and they go to the kitchen and bring it back, you don't need to know how the kitchen works. um, try to avoid technical terms and check if they're following.
Tell me about a technical decision you made where you were choosing between two reasonable options.
We had to choose between two frameworks and I researched both and made a comparison, and we picked the one that was better for our use case and had more community support.
Tell me about the hardest bug you have had to track down. What made it hard?
I had a bug once that was really hard because the error message wasn't helpful. you know, i used the debugger and stepped through the code until I found where it was going wrong, and then fixed it.
